In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,
2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, and 2521, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being broadcast via
teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council Chambers, or virtually in the
meeting in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 9128) from any phone, Meeting ID:
848 7015 4176 Passcode: 443943. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call in option from
a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00
p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the Planning Commission for their consideration and
included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 848 7015 4176 Passcode: 443943.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are available on
the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 6, 2022

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274, and via teleconference pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR SCHACHTER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler

  Commissioners Absent:  Carman

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JULY 11, 2022

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220196; LOCATION: 40 DAPPLEGRAY LANE;
  APPLICANT: LOUIE TOMARO; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-220197) for the demolition of an existing single-family residence and
  detached stable, and the construction of a new, 3,229 sq.ft. split-level single-family
  residence and attached two-car garage. The proposal also includes a Grading application
  (G-220198) for the exportation of 186 cubic yards of earth material associated with the
  construction of the new home.

Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220196
summarizing the staff report.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-220196, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220197) for a split-level home
featuring an attached two-car garage, a second-story deck, covered patio, and Grading
application (G-220198), subject to the conditions of approval in the staff report.

CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about the requirement to maintain 800 sq. ft. for future horse
keeping area. Associate Planner Flores stated that this is required since this property is in the
Horse Overlay Zone.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 6, 2022
  1
 Mr. Louie Tomaro, Architect, stated that the house will be built closer to the street; however, the
rear portion will be built close to its current location; there is a substantial front yard proposed to
be used to make the home larger. The stable which is currently in the rear of the property will be
removed and the area will remain open for a future horse keeping area.

Mr. Kirk Retz expressed his strong support for this project and stated that this home will be a great
improvement to the neighborhood.

COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he noticed that he is not building the house as forward as
his neighbors and this is a great overall project.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that it has great curb appeal and appreciates the front
setback.

COMMISSIONER OLSON AND VICE CHAIR YOO concurred.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE PA-220196, A NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY DETERMINATION (NC-
  220197) FOR A SPLIT-LEVEL HOME FEATURING AN ATTACHED TWO-CAR
  GARAGE, A SECOND-STORY DECK, COVERED PATIO, AND GRADING
  APPLICATION (G-220198), SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL IN THE
  STAFF REPORT.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Carman
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission approved Planning Application No. 220196.
There is a 20-day appeal period by where any member of the public may appeal this project to
the City Council.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220241; ADDRESS: 19 BUCKSKIN LANE;
  APPLICANT: DAVID & HELEN SHAW; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-220242) to legalize two unpermitted detached accessory
  structures built less than 7’ away from a bridle trail. A Variance (V-2202423) is required to
  consider an application for building a structure less than 7’ to a bridle trail per RHEMC
  Section 17.06.330. The proposal also includes a grading application (G-220244) for on-
  site grading greater than 3’ or 20 cubic yards of earth movement.

Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220241
summarizing the staff report.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the
public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; and direct staff to prepare a resolution
denying both Variance Application V-220243 and Neighborhood Compatibility Determination NC-
220242, requiring the applicant to demolish or relocate the unpermitted accessory structure to
comply with the code; and, approve Grading Application G-220244.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

David Shaw, 2715 Palos Verdes Drive North and 19 Buckskin Lane, provided background on both
properties. He stated that the structures in question were built on foundations of structures that
existed when he bought the property and were subsequently demolished. Mr. Shaw stated that,
at the time of initiating construction of the structures, he was not aware that a permit would be
required since he intended to build structures (a tack room and hay storage shed) under 120 sq.
ft. and under the height limit. However, he added a tree house with a deck above the hay storage
shed and a separate tack room. Mr. Shaw also presented a slide with the retaining wall that was
built and explained that it now has drainage, gravel, and drywells so that when it rains the water
will go back into the dirt naturally. He stated that the only issue is the 7’ setback requirement; he
disagreed that there is no hardship since tearing them down would be terrible and it is not possible
to relocate the structures. He also added that the trail behind his property is 25’ wide. He stated

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 6, 2022
  2
 that there is no harm or safety issues with keeping the structures. He also stated that the
easements are being maintained.

Mr. Retz stated that he is in support of the Variance. He stated that he has been walking the trails
for a couple of decades and stated that the structures that were originally there were dilapidated;
he stated that he likes the improvements that have been made to the structures. He also stated
that previously when it rained, the trail was impassible and since Mr. Shaw moved in, the trail has
improved significantly. He stated that Mr. Shaw is a good neighbor who has improved the
neighborhood. He expressed his strong support of a Variance for this project.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the existing building pads where the structures were
built. Director Wahba stated that the existing buildings did not have the benefit of permits and
stated that he believes that the building pads have been repoured and elevated.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHACHTER, Director Wahba stated that sometimes there
is miscommunication between planning and building and safety in regard to structures under 120
sq. ft. Although a 120 sq. ft. single story structure may be exempt from a building permit; it is not
exempt from zoning. He added that City Hall was open during the COVID shutdown and permits
could be issued. Mr. Wahba stated that although these structures are beautiful from a
Neighborhood Compatibility standpoint; the problem is the 7’ setback requirement from the trail
easement that neither structure meets.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that from the photographs, the original structures were “garden
shed” type portable structures.

CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that approving this would set a precedent for other similar projects.

VICE CHAIR YOO stated that he sympathizes with Mr. Shaw’s predicament, but there is no legal
basis to approve this Variance.

In response to a question by VICE CHAIR YOO, Director Wahba stated that the concrete pads
on-grade are not an issue; the structures do not meet the 7’ setback.

COMMISSIONER LOW asked if there have been any similar situations where a Variance has
been approved. Director Wahba stated that properties where the Variance findings were met, and
a qualifying physical hardship could be demonstrated, then an approval could be granted. The
City is not aware of any other Variances being granted in the neighborhood for a reduction in a
bridle trail easement setback.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO PREPARE A RESOLUTION DENYING BOTH VARIANCE
  APPLICATION V-220243 AND NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY DETERMINATION
  NC-220242, AND APPROVING GRADING APPLICATION G-220244.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Carman
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that the staff will prepare a resolution denying Variance Application No. V-
220243 and Neighborhood Compatibility Determination NC-220242 and recommending approval
of Grading Application No. G-220244 for approval by the Planning Commission at its next meeting
on October 3, 2022.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220190; ADDRESS: 58 SILVER SADDLE LANE;
  APPLICANT: PRAVEEN GATTU; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-220191) for the construction of a new 2,743 sq.ft. deck
  at the rear of the house where a portion of the deck is detached and will be constructed
  on a hillside. The proposal also includes a Variance application (V-220192) for the length
  of the deck exceeding 50% of the width of the lot.

Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220190

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 6, 2022
  3
 summarizing the staff report. Two attached patio covers are being proposed as part of this
application.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the
public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
Resolution No. 220190, approving the project subject to the conditions of approval.

COMMISSIONER EDLER asked if a new permit would be required to enclose the patio covers.
Associate Planner Flores stated that this would require a permit since it may constitute living area
and would need to meet zoning and building code requirements.

COMMISSIONER LOW asked if there is a photo of what is existing in this area now. Director
Wahba stated that there is no useable backyard for this lot, which is also a similar condition on
the immediately adjacent properties as well

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

Praveen Gattu, Property Owner 58 Silver Saddle Lane, stated that the usable area of the property
is very small; he had considered to stay within the code, however, the deck would look like it is
partially cutoff; and there is a privacy issue that this deck may resolve.

CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that there is a neighbor who suggested a tree be planted and asked
if that would be agreeable to Mr. Gattu. Director Wahba stated that this would be planted at the
toe of the slope on Shady Vista. He stated that the Parks and Activities Commission would
typically consider the type of tree to be planted in that area to make sure that it is consistent with
the City’s tree planting list. Also, normally a hillside deck project is not conditioned to provide
complete privacy to the home below, particularly to yard areas

A brief discussion ensued about the privacy concerns.

Tony Williams, 6 Shady Vista Road, stated that there is a privacy issue. He stated that his
acceptance was based on the condition that a tree could be planted in the course of the project.
Mr. Gattu stated that they would also like to address the privacy issue and stated that they have
paid for and planted six trees and the city paid and planted one tree. The trees are not doing well
since the slope was reinforced with a soil and concrete mixture. Mr. Gattu stated that in good faith
they will do what they can, but do not believe this should be a condition of approval. He added
that they will be adding trees at the edge of the hillside deck to camouflage the foundation.

Mr. Williams stated that he is concerned with the intention of the agreement. He stated that he
requested that a 20’-25’ mature tree be planted in line with the existing trees.

A brief discussion ensued regarding the feasibility of where to plant the tree.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked if the size of this deck is common. Director Wahba stated that the size
of this deck is not uncommon, however, there have not been many hillside decks of this size built
in the city.

A brief discussion ensued about the size of the deck.

Director Wahba stated that he does not believe this will set a precedent since this is a unique
situation where a deck of this size is warranted in order to have a usable backyard area.

CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that for Neighborhood Compatibility, there are no other decks; scale,
it may be a little large; and privacy, the tree proposed by Mr. Williams may resolve this issue.

COMMISSIONER YOO stated that Mr. Williams has appropriate privacy concerns.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion to,

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 6, 2022
  4
   ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-220190, APPROVING THE VARIANCE WITH THE
  CONDITION THAT A MATURE TREE, AS APPROVED BY STAFF, BE PLANTED IN
  LINE WITH THE EXISTING TREES WITH A $10K MAXIMUM EXPENSE.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if he would be in agreement with a maximum $10K expense for the
tree. Mr. Gattu agreed to a $10K maximum expense.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTIN NO. PA-220190, APPROVING THE VARIANCE WITH THE
  CONDITION THAT A MATURE TREE, AS APPROVED BY STAFF, BE PLANTED IN
  LINE WITH THE EXISTING TREES WITH A $10K MAXIMUM EXPENSE.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Carman
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission approved Resolution No. 220190. A
condition will be added to the resolution to require that the applicant work with the city to have a
mature tree planted in the public right-of-way along Shady Vista with a cap of $10K that the
applicant will contribute. There is a 20-day appeal period by where any member of the public may
appeal this project to the City Council.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220326; ADDRESS: Citywide; APPLICANT: City of
  Rolling Hills Estates; DESCRIPTION: A Public Hearing for the Planning Commission to
  consider proposed municipal code amendments regarding: (1) Update to Chapter 17.76
  (Density Bonus and Other Incentives) to address changes in state law; (2) Amendments
  to Chapter 17.30 (Commercial-General District) to provide for bonus level development in
  exchange for the provision of certain community amenities or benefits; and (3) a new
  Chapter 17.82 (Development Agreements), which provides procedures for the application,
  review, approval and monitoring of negotiated agreements with the city regarding
  development projects. A recommendation on the municipal code amendments will be
  made by the Planning Commission to the City Council for consideration at a future City
  Council meeting.

Director Wahba provided a summary of the staff report and stated that these are implementation
measures from the Land Use and Housing Elements of the General Plan Update.

Director Wahba stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission conduct the public
hearing on the proposed zoning code amendments; provide any comments on the proposed
zoning code amendments for City Council consideration; and adopt Resolution No. PA-220326
recommending approval of the zoning code amendments to the City Council.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMIONER MEDAWAR asked how this will impact the retail aspect and is mixed-use still part
of this. Director Wahba stated that there is a mixed-use overlay implemented as part of the last
two General Plan updates and that his will continue to be implemented. There had been
discussion of coming up with a mandated percentage of retail as part of a mixed-use project. This
is still a discretionary action as part of the conditional use permit process, where the percentages
of uses to be mixed will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Having a community benefit
ordinance provides additional tools to make sure that there is a balance between residential and

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 6, 2022
  5
 retail, and that the community is gaining additional public benefits from a project.

CHAIR SCHACHTER expressed concern with the applicant submitting their own appraisal report.
Director Wahba stated that the city has the ability to have the appraisal reviewed by a third party
at the applicant’s expense.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. PA-220326 RECOMMENDING APPROVAL OF THE
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENTS TO THE CITY COUNCIL.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
NOES:
ABSENT: Carman
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission approved Resolution No. 220326,
recommending approval of the zoning code amendments to the City Council. The zoning code
amendments will be presented to the City Council for their review and approval on September 27,
2022.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired on the status of the substandard property on Santa Bella.
Director Wahba stated that he will follow up on this.

COMMISSIONER OLSON inquired about who is handling Code Enforcement. Director Wahba
stated that interviews for a Code Compliance Officer will be held soon; Planning staff is handling
code enforcement at this time.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  None.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – JULY 26, 2022

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – AUGUST 23, 2022

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Schachter, Chair
